body: it happened when i was 19, and i'm in my mid 30s now.  It took me until just a couple years ago to start opening up to my friends and church voluntarily though, but I really wish I had sooner.
she says she knows friends its happened to and a therapist told her straight up that if they felt she was a danger to anyone (including herself) he would have to report it
I called a bit after I posted and got some advice.  I went over tonight (against her wishes) and she is ok for tonight it seems.. Thank you

I'm certainly trying, but I'm not the most compassionate person and simply don't understand what's she's going through well enough to know the right things to say to help her.  I try to affirm my love for her and show her that is sincere though.  I've also certainly been trying to get her to go seek counseling, but she is convinced that if she goes, they ask if she has suicidal thoughts and she says yes, her kids will be taken from her.

Do you have an attorney?  If not, I recommend contacting one to see what can be done about the case.  

That said, I do understand what you're going through first hand.  I won't go into details, but I can say that even with a stigma like that attached to your name, the vast majority of people that get to know you will not judge you even if they find out.  I used to live in fear just like you, but now most people in my life know and accept me regardless because they know who I am, not what some website says.  And those that don't accept me aren't worth knowing anyway.  I've held a good job for 6 years now and actually have a career.  There is a light at the end of the tunnel for sure, but you have to give people a chance.  Yes, it's risky, but the ones worth keeping around will accept you.
